you_should_know.title: See email called "smoking gun" in Colorado's lawsuit alleging White House retaliation, White House denies tie to Tina Peters
you_should_know.summary: Colorado's lawsuit alleging that the Trump administration retaliated against the state came into sharper focus as court records emerged. The state says the administration targeted it with funding cuts after Gov. Polis refused to pardon Tina Peters, the former clerk of Mesa County in western Colorado, whose prosecution over election policies is central to the case. A judge ordered documents released, and attorneys for the state pointed to a newly uncovered White House email - described in new exhibits as a "smoking gun" - as key evidence of what the suit calls an unconstitutional scheme to punish the state. The White House denies any tie to Peters.
you_should_know.description: New exhibits in the federal court case Colorado vs. Trump, which alleges the Trump administration orchestrated an "unconstitutional scheme to attack and punish the state," reveal communications between the White House and federal agencies on the topic of Colorado.
